text:
alice (customer): Hey team — since last night's maintenance our app is seeing p99 jumps on /v1/generate in us-west-2, tail ~800ms (used to be ~120ms). request-id: req_9f2a. No obvious 5xx, just long waits. Can someone triage?

maria (support): Sorry for the trouble, escalated to infra. Can you share a couple more request-ids and the approximate timestamps? Any request logs?

alice (customer): Sure: req_9f2a, req_9f3b, req_9f7c. Timestamps around 02:12–02:18 UTC. No error body, just timeouts/504s for some requests. Dedicated hosts only.

maria (support): pinging eng-runtime and eng-infra @jonas @tara — adding traces attached by customer.

jonas (eng-runtime): on it. From the trace for req_9f2a I see a big stall inside token generation step, then a long wait in the host (syscall) before GPU resumes. Do we have host dmesg for the affected host?

maria (support): pasted customer's dmesg excerpt into the thread.

jonas (eng-runtime): I'm seeing repeated kernel logs that look like UVM faults + page fault handling spikes. Sample from affected host:
```
[ 1412.123456] NVRM: UVM: vm_fault for VA 0x7f8d... status=0x2
[ 1412.123459] uvm: major fault 0.45s, handle_page_faults()
[ 1412.123470] nvme0n1: io 0x... queued, qdepth 256->512, nvme_io_wait
```
This pattern aligns with heavy major faults causing NVMe queue depth and iowait spikes.

tara (eng-infra): we rolled kernel 5.15.x and driver 525.xx in last night's maintenance window. Correlation looks strong: hosts with newer driver show pagefault storms and nvme qdepth surges starting at 02:13UTC. Might be a UVM pinning/regression in this driver/kernel combo.

devon (eng-sre): I've pulled disk metrics: NVMe qdepth and avg latency spike exactly at the p99 spike windows. Host iowait climbs, overall p95 also nudges up. Plotting per-host heatmap now.

jonas (eng-runtime): repro plan: 1) enable UVM debug logging on a repro host, 2) run synthetic load hitting large context-window models to trigger large VRAM+UVM working sets, 3) collect /proc/vmstat, dmesg, and nvme top metrics. If we confirm UVM major faults, fallback to non-UVM path in runtime.

tara (eng-infra): immediate mitigations we can offer customers: A) temporary rollback to driver 520.40 (previous stable) across affected Dedicated hosts, or B) set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_UVM=1 env on runtime to disable unified-memory prefetching and force non-UVM allocations. Both have tradeoffs (rollback timeline vs memory pressure).

maria (support): sent mitigation options to customer with steps to set the env var and instructions for requesting a controlled driver rollback. Customer asked for fastest fix.

alice (customer): trying env var now on two hosts. Will report in ~10m. Thanks.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued #789 — fleet rollback estimated 3.5h to complete (manual approval required).

devon (eng-sre): I'll monitor p99/p95 for user traffic and NVMe qdepth for the next 6 hours. If env var works, we can advise customers while infra coordinates rollback and vendor bug filing.

jonas (eng-runtime): short-term runtime tweak: reduce concurrent model workers per GPU from 4 -> 2 on repro hosts to reduce concurrent UVM fault pressure while we gather traces. Pushing a config change to test group now.

tara (eng-infra): long-term: file detailed bug with driver vendor including kernel traces, uvm logs, and repro workload. Also evaluating kernel tuning (reduce max_map_count? pre-pinning heuristics?) but need vendor input before broad changes.

maria (support): customer update: "applied REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_UVM=1 to two hosts — both show p99 down to ~140ms within 8 minutes." Customer: :raised_hands:

alice (customer): Confirmed — env var fixed the tail for now. Please keep me posted on rollback schedule or vendor fix.

devon (eng-sre): noted. I'll open an incident follow-up doc with RCA checklist and attach traces. Tagging this for on-call review in morning handoff.

jonas (eng-runtime): follow-ups for runtime: add health check to detect UVM-major-fault storms (majflt rate) and auto-toggle disable-uvm fallback.

tara (eng-infra): follow-ups for infra: coordinate driver rollback plan for critical clouds, compile repro case for vendor, and add NVMe qdepth alerting tied to UVM fault signals.

maria (support): closing loop with customer for now; will reopen if they see regressions after fleet changes. Good job team.
